public_rationale: The qualitative comparison holds. Slack's documented deployment shows AWS supplying computing resources for an AI product. Amazon reported demand for training and inference chips, while NVIDIA reported strong demand for its computing platform. Both occupied the supplier role described in the passage. This does not establish that their businesses were identical or that most AWS AI revenue came from experimentation.
limitations: No infrastructure revenue share is established.
AWS also offered application-layer AI products.
The records include production use, so they do not establish that customers were merely experimenting.
Amazon's earnings remarks were read through a clearly identified transcript reproduction.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In essence, Amazon is benefitting from AI in much the same way NVIDIA is, by supplying the compute people need while working out what AI is useful for.

statement.excerpt: In essence, Amazon is benefitting from AI in much the same way NVIDIA is.

from_speaker: in much the same way NVIDIA is
they need cloud compute to do so
our_interpretation: The surrounding passage makes this a comparison of supplier roles: AWS and NVIDIA benefit from customers needing computing infrastructure to develop and run AI.
The sentence does not specify equal revenues, margins, growth rates or business models.
It does not explicitly assert that all, or a measured majority, of either company's AI business comes from experimentation.
For the ongoing state, use the latest reported operating quarters available before the post: the April–June calendar quarter and the corresponding fiscal-quarter reporting window through July.
This is a qualitative business-model observation, not a claim about a specified monetary amount.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous disclosures show actual customer use or demand for AWS computing services and NVIDIA computing products to develop or operate AI.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous evidence shows that the proposed computing-supplier benefit did not exist for one of the companies, or that the claimed similarity depends on a materially false description of its offerings.
